finding.title: deadline not set when swapping with uniswapV3. 0 amount as deadline will always revert.

judge_and_sponsor_statements.author: alex-ppg
judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
The Warden's submission specifies that the absence of an explicit value for the deadline argument of the referenced structs will initialize their value to 0.

As evidenced by PeripheryValidation::checkDeadline in Uniswap V3 (example of ETH deployment), the transaction would fail as "expired". This means that all exact input/output swaps performed by the contract would result in failure. I believe a severity of High is appropriate and invite the Sponsor to re-visit.

triage_prose:
The Warden's submission specifies that the absence of an explicit value for the deadline argument of the referenced structs will initialize their value to 0.

As evidenced by PeripheryValidation::checkDeadline in Uniswap V3 (example of ETH deployment), the transaction would fail as "expired". This means that all exact input/output swaps performed by the contract would result in failure. I believe a severity of High is appropriate and invite the Sponsor to re-visit.

original_claim_body: Protocol signer's signature can be replayed When a lender has multiple similar pay orders that correspond to the same metadata hash and a renter is provided with a protocol signer's signature for fulfilling one of these pay orders, the renter is able to replay such signature to fulfill other pay orders of the lender as long as the renter uses the same safe and such signature is not expired. The second option would be to check the values returned by morphoBlue.withdraw and sanity check them to ensure slippage is within acceptable bounds.

submission_issue_comments.author: 0jovi0
submission_issue_comments.body:
Hey, how's it going?

Issues #830 and #831 are duplicates of one another, and issue #824 is a separate finding. Those issues are not duplicates of #991.
Here's my reasoning:
 According to C4 documentation:
Findings are duplicates if they share the same root cause.

More specifically, if fixing the Root Cause (in a reasonable manner) would cause the finding to no longer be exploitable, then the findings are duplicates.


For the issues mentioned, fixing one issue does not fix the other at all. If it wasn't reported, the protocol would be left exposed to slippage on other parts of its connectors. Duplicating the issues with the lack of slippage control with other protocol integrations is misleading as the sponsor may end up believing the issue is a single one and fix one part of the codebase while leaving many other parts exposed. 

 
 Acknowledging no slippage control at the protocol as a single root cause is a false premise. 
The protocol does know about slippage and also implements protection on some of its connectors. 
Examples: 
The UNIV3Connector within its usage of the MintParams struct at at and at .

The BaseConnector acknowledges slippage checks on its dev comments: 

 Issue #1018 is a different Pendle slippage issue that is not a duplicate of #991.
Issues 830 and 831 are relative to MorphoConnector slippage, 824 is relative to Aave slippage and neither have been submitted elsewhere.

Thanks for your time!

If one sets shares to zero when calling withdraw; the order is a market order, as he/she currently holds no assets, meaning it accepts whatever conversion rate the market offers and burns the required shares without user-controlled input. If one sets assets to zero in the same context; the order is a limit order, as he/she holds shares and can fine tune the maximum amount of shares that can be taken away, limiting risk-exposure mainly to price-manipulation attack vectors.

submission_issue_comments.author: 0xAlix2
submission_issue_comments.body:
Hello @gzeon-c4, thanks for judging this!

I agree that the root cause for this is OOS, however, this is critically affecting the whole protocol, as the whole TVL calculation will be blocked, and the TX will always revert with an overflow. So it doesn't affect just the Uniswap connector or the connector's TVL.

As a result, I believe this should be valid.

Thanks!

submission_issue_comments.author: 0xAlix2
submission_issue_comments.body:
Hello @gzeon-c4, thanks for re-evaluating this!

A couple of notes:
 I believe this should be high as it DOSes the whole protocol.
 This still has the downgraded by judge and insufficient quality report, which I believe could affect the rewards calculation. 

thanks!

submission_issue_comments.author: DadeKuma
submission_issue_comments.body:
@gzeon-c4 
 My reasoning for insufficient quality:

 Verdict: Fault in out-of-scope library, impact in in-scope contract, to reward or not to reward
 We would like to clarify the situation where an in-scope contract composes/inherits with an OOS contract, and the root cause exists in the OOS contract. In such cases, the finding is to be treated as OOS, while exceptional scenarios are at the discretion of the judge.

 

Even if valid, the root cause is definitely in the OOS contract (even if it affects in-scope contracts), and the mitigation must be made in the OOS contract.

finding.summary: Impact: Minimal transaction timing protection Location: Launchpad.sol - AMM interaction functions Description: Both addLiquidity() and swapTokensForExactTokens() use block.timestamp or block.timestamp + 1 as deadlines, providing insufficient protection against transaction timing manipulation. Issues: block.timestamp as deadline offers no protection block.timestamp + 1 provides minimal protection (1 second) Transactions can be delayed by miners/validators without meaningful constraints Recommendation: Use more reasonable deadline windows (e.g., block.timestamp + 300 for 5 minutes).
finding.title: Hardcoded Deadline in AMM Operations

setMarkPrice() function is called every second or every 5 - 10 seconds doesn’t make much of a difference for this attack path, as a malicious user will have to submit orders that expire in the next block and cancel them in the next block.

finding.author: 0xAsen
finding.author_note: handle from the report's 'Submitted by' line
finding.root_cause:
(1) Caller-conditioned initialization in the factory
 [code] 
A non-Launchpad caller produces a pair permanently initialized with lp = 0, dist = 0, and locks it as canonical.
(2) Hard gating in the pair
 [code] 
With launchpadFeeDistributor == 0, the pair never computes Launchpad fees and never calls distributeLaunchpadFees.
finding.severity_source: final report section heading (H-xx / M-xx)
finding.summary: launchpad/uniswap/GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory.sol #L36-L37 The factory initializes Launchpad fee hooks (launchpadLp, launchpadFeeDistributor) only when createPair(tokenA, tokenB) is called by the Launchpad.
